findings.text: System call entry for seccomp control delegates all work to a shared dispatcher that interprets operation numbers and validates associated flags and arguments.

The shared dispatcher supports strict installation, filter installation, action availability query, and notification size query. Strict installation requires empty flags and no argument. Availability and size queries require empty flags. Unknown operations fail as invalid.

Privilege control entry maps strict mode and filter mode to the corresponding dispatcher operations with empty flags. Strict mode forces an empty argument to satisfy internal checks. Other modes fail as invalid.
Mode query reports the current execution context mode value without side effects.

Permission check dispatches on the current mode. Suspended tracing under checkpoint restore support bypasses evaluation. Strict mode invokes strict handling and permits continuation. Filter mode evaluates rule sets. Dead mode warns and terminates with an uncatchable signal. Unknown modes trap.
Error outcomes are bounded above by a maximum error value and suppress the underlying request while recording the decision. The bound prevents out of range status values from escaping to user space.
Trap outcomes preserve the original register view for diagnostics and deliver a synchronous system signal carrying filter supplied detail, with the request suppressed and the decision recorded.

Trace outcomes depend on tracer interest and liveness. Without interest the request is suppressed as unavailable. With interest an event carrying filter detail is offered. Fatal distress or a withdrawn number causes suppression. A changed number is reevaluated under trace aware rules without duplicate suppression accounting.
User notification outcomes delegate the continuation choice to a cooperating handler. Handler acceptance permits continuation while other handler dispositions suppress the request.
Logging and allowance both permit continuation. Logging additionally records the decision. Allowance implies no retained matching rule.

Kill outcomes for thread scope, process scope, and unknown results are terminal. They mark the context dead and record the event. Single thread termination or process scope termination presents original registers and forces a dumping signal. Multithreaded thread scope termination exits the calling thread directly. The request is never continued.

Forced seccomp signals are synchronous system signals that identify the offending call number and architecture, point at the call site, and carry the filter supplied reason as associated detail. The caller selects dumping versus nondumping termination.

Strict installation is allowed only when assignment rules permit. It executes atomically with signal handling state and optionally disables timestamp counting where the platform supports that feature.

Filter installation rejects unknown flag bits. It rejects combined thread synchronization and listener creation without explicit tolerance for missing threads. It rejects killable receive without listener creation. Rule set preparation completes before any dossier locks are taken.

At most one active notification channel may exist along the installed chain. An installation that would create a second channel fails as busy. The check requires protection against concurrent thread synchronization.

Listener creation assigns an unpredictable initial identity, initializes an empty pending list, publishes a dedicated file with readiness, release, and control operations, and holds a reference. Success installs the descriptor and reports it. Failure drops the file, releases the descriptor, and detaches the channel.

Channel detachment unblocks every pending waiter that lacks an answer by marking it answered with unavailable status and waking it, then releases channel memory. Release combines detachment with reference drop.

The notification mutex serializes the pending list, per request state and outcome fields, channel flags, and file injection queues. Identity lookup requires the mutex to be held. Receive, send, validity, flag update, injection, readiness, and detach paths all hold it, with interruptible acquisition where user context may need to abort waiting.

The signal handling spin lock with interrupt exclusion serializes mode assignment and duplicate channel checks. Thread wide installation additionally holds the credential guard mutex in killable form across assignment to exclude concurrent execution identity changes.

Reception waiting uses a dedicated queue with selective wakeups limited to input, error, and hangup interest, combined with a pending request counter and a live user count. Zero users or an available count avoids sleeping. Sleeping is interruptible.

Observed linkage shows a rule set pointing to a previous rule set, a channel object, a notification mutex, a wait queue, and a user count. The channel object holds a pending list, a request counter, flags, and a next identity value. Each pending entry holds identity, state, outcome status and value, handler flags, owning task reference, captured call data, completion, injection list, and list linkage.

Observed exchange shapes carry identity, process identity, and captured call data from kernel to handler, and identity plus outcome status, value, and continuation request from handler to kernel. File injection carries source descriptor, target descriptor detail, option flags, and size versioning. Size discovery reports the three exchange sizes.

Pending requests move from initial to sent when handed to a handler and then to replied upon handler answer or channel teardown. A failed handoff to user space can return a sent entry to initial with accounting restored. Only sent entries accept answers or file injection, and at most one answer is accepted.

Execution contexts occupy strict, filter, or dead modes. Strict delegates to dedicated handling. Filter evaluates rule sets. Dead is terminal and forces immediate termination if ever reentered. Mode queries report the current value.
Unknown modes and unknown filter outcomes trap or warn and terminate rather than permitting continuation. Survival past a kill outcome is treated as a defect.

Fatal distress racing tracer delivery suppresses the request to let termination proceed. Interrupted file injection either observes completion or cleanly unqueues. Copy failures to user space restore pending state and accounting rather than losing the request. Detachment during waiting wakes with unavailable status.

Supported filter result names are SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW, SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO, SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS, SECCOMP_RET_KILL_THREAD, SECCOMP_RET_LOG, SECCOMP_RET_TRACE, SECCOMP_RET_TRAP, SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF. Unknown values are reported as unsupported.

Known execution modes are SECCOMP_MODE_DEAD, SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER, SECCOMP_MODE_STRICT. Known dispatcher operations are SECCOMP_GET_ACTION_AVAIL, SECCOMP_GET_NOTIF_SIZES, SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER, SECCOMP_SET_MODE_STRICT.

Known notification control commands are SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_SET_FLAGS, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ID_VALID, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ID_VALID_WRONG_DIR, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_SEND, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_RECV.
Known notification and injection option names are SECCOMP_ADDFD_FLAG_SEND, SECCOMP_ADDFD_FLAG_SETFD, SECCOMP_USER_NOTIF_FLAG_CONTINUE, SECCOMP_USER_NOTIF_FD_SYNC_WAKE_UP.

Known filter installation flag names are SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_MASK, SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER, SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC, SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC_ESRCH, SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_WAIT_KILLABLE_RECV, plus O_CLOEXEC.
The notification file exposes readiness polling, release cleanup, and control operations for receive, send, validity, flag update, and file injection with extensible sizing.
Readiness reports input when any entry awaits handoff, output when any entry awaits answer, and hangup when no users remain. Waiting for readiness uses the channel queue.

Reception requires a zeroed extensibility area, waits for demand, publishes one initial entry as sent, and wakes writers. Failure to deliver to user space restores the entry to initial and restores accounting and input readiness.

Answering requires known flags only, with continuation exclusive of status and value. Unknown identity fails as missing while duplicate or mistimed answers fail as in progress. Accepted answers store outcome and wake the waiter, optionally with processor local wake semantics.
Validity checks report success only for sent entries and missing otherwise. Flag updates accept only the synchronous wake option and fail otherwise.

File injection validates size bounds and versioned copying, restricts descriptor options and control flags, requires explicit targeting when a target number is given, and requires the target request to be in sent state. Combined injection plus answer requires an empty injection queue and consumes the single allowed answer. Busy, missing, or mistimed targets are rejected. Interruption either observes completion or cleanly unqueues.
Size discovery reports the kernel sizes of the notification, answer, and captured data shapes, failing only on copy faults.
Control dispatch separates fixed size operations from extensible ones by masking direction and size bits before matching file injection. Unknown commands fail as invalid.
Identity lookup scans the pending list under lock and distinguishes missing identities from present ones.
Alternate configurations without filter support fail installation as invalid and trap on evaluation instead of enforcing rules.
